probes.summary: Verified the declared data links, AS identities, two established eBGP sessions, exact /32 origin and learning paths, FIB installation, and bidirectional source-preserving transit.
Verified coherent FRR/SONiC and Ubuntu routing state, no static bypasses or IPv4 NAT, expected transit filtering, no active capture residue, and persistent configuration references.
limitations: Reboot persistence was assessed from saved configuration and current service state; reboot was not performed by the read-only authored plan.

assertions.summary: Both declared eBGP sessions are established with the correct ASes. Node2 originates only 198.18.201.2/32, node3 originates only 198.18.202.3/32, node1 learns each through the correct peer and installs both routes in the FIB.

evidence.command: command -v vtysh; vtysh -c 'show ip bgp summary'; vtysh -c 'show ip bgp 198.18.201.2/32'; vtysh -c 'show ip bgp 198.18.202.3/32'; vtysh -c 'show ip route 198.18.201.2/32'; vtysh -c 'show ip route 198.18.202.3/32'
evidence.observation: BGP local AS 65100. Neighbors 10.91.0.10/65101 and 10.92.0.10/65102 are both established with PfxRcd/PfxSnt 1. 198.18.201.2/32 is learned via 10.91.0.10 and installed via eth1; 198.18.202.3/32 is learned via 10.92.0.10 and installed via eth2. Each route is advertised toward the opposite peer.

evidence.command: vtysh -c 'show ip bgp summary'; vtysh -c 'show ip bgp 198.18.201.2/32'; vtysh -c 'show ip bgp 198.18.202.3/32'; vtysh -c 'show ip route 198.18.201.2/32'; vtysh -c 'show ip route 198.18.202.3/32'
evidence.observation: BGP local AS 65101; neighbor 10.91.0.254/65100 established with one prefix received and one sent. 198.18.201.2/32 is Local, sourced from 0.0.0.0, directly connected on lo; 198.18.202.3/32 is learned with path 65100 65102 via 10.91.0.254 and installed via enp8s0.

evidence.command: vtysh -c 'show ip bgp summary'; vtysh -c 'show ip bgp 198.18.202.3/32'; vtysh -c 'show ip bgp 198.18.201.2/32'; vtysh -c 'show ip route 198.18.202.3/32'; vtysh -c 'show ip route 198.18.201.2/32'
evidence.observation: BGP local AS 65102; neighbor 10.92.0.254/65100 established with one prefix received and one sent. 198.18.202.3/32 is Local, sourced from 0.0.0.0, directly connected on lo; 198.18.201.2/32 is learned with path 65100 65101 via 10.92.0.254 and installed via enp8s0.

assertions.summary: Both endpoint-sourced directions succeeded through the declared data links. Narrow captures on node1 eth1 and eth2 showed unchanged endpoint source and destination addresses in both directions, with no packet drops.

evidence.observation: Route selection was via 10.91.0.254 dev enp8s0. Three probes sourced from 198.18.201.2 reached 198.18.202.3 with 0% loss.
Route selection was via 10.92.0.254 dev enp8s0. Three probes sourced from 198.18.202.3 reached 198.18.201.2 with 0% loss.

evidence.command: D=$(mktemp -d /tmp/sonic-bgp.XXXXXX) || exit 1; tcpdump -i eth1 -nn -l 'icmp and host 198.18.201.2 and host 198.18.202.3' > "$D/eth1.txt" 2>&1 & P1=$!; tcpdump -i eth2 -nn -l 'icmp and host 198.18.201.2 and host 198.18.202.3' > "$D/eth2.txt" 2>&1 & P2=$!; sleep 1; printf 'capture_dir=%s\ncapture_pids=%s,%s\n' "$D" "$P1" "$P2"
evidence.observation: Independent narrow captures were started on node1 eth1 and eth2.

evidence.command:
kill 13592 13593 2>/dev/null || true; sleep 1; printf '%s
' '--- eth1 capture ---'; sed -n '1,80p' /tmp/sonic-bgp.pJkJt6/eth1.txt 2>/dev/null; printf '%s
' '--- eth2 capture ---'; sed -n '1,80p' /tmp/sonic-bgp.pJkJt6/eth2.txt 2>/dev/null; printf '%s
' '--- data counters ---'; ip -s link show dev eth1; ip -s link show dev eth2; rm -f /tmp/sonic-bgp.pJkJt6/eth1.txt /tmp/sonic-bgp.pJkJt6/eth2.txt; rmdir /tmp/sonic-bgp.pJkJt6 2>/dev/null || true; printf '%s
' 'capture_cleanup=complete'
evidence.observation: Both eth1 and eth2 captured all 12 filtered packets: requests and replies retained 198.18.201.2 and 198.18.202.3 as the original endpoints in both directions. Each capture reported 0 packets dropped; interface counters reported zero errors/drops. Temporary captures and processes were removed.

assertions.summary: Task-owned routing and FRR state is coherent and persistent: no static or management bypass routes, no docker0 leakage, expected forwarding/filtering, matching saved FRR configuration, and no active evaluator capture residue. SONiC baseline health artifacts were not treated as executor defects.

evidence.command:
printf '%s
' '--- routing/state ---'; ip -4 addr; ip route show table all; ip rule show; printf '%s
' '--- static routes ---'; ip route show proto static; printf '%s
' '--- forwarding ---'; sysctl net.ipv4.ip_forward net.ipv4.conf.all.forwarding net.ipv4.conf.eth1.forwarding net.ipv4.conf.eth2.forwarding net.ipv4.conf.all.rp_filter; printf '%s
' '--- FRR config ---'; vtysh -c 'show running-config' | grep -E '^(router bgp| bgp router-id| no bgp| neighbor (10\.91\.0\.10|10\.92\.0\.10)| address-family| network| route-map| ip prefix-list| exit-address-family|!)'; printf '%s
' '--- services/listeners ---'; systemctl --failed --no-legend; systemctl is-active frr 2>/dev/null; ss -ltnp; printf '%s
' '--- SONiC containers ---'; docker ps --format '{{.Names}} {{.Status}}' 2>/dev/null; printf '%s
' '--- evaluator residue/debug ---'; pgrep -a -f '[t]cpdump|[s]trace|[g]db|[t]shark' 2>/dev/null; find /tmp -maxdepth 1 \( -name 'sonic-bgp*' -o -name '*bgp*' \) -print 2>/dev/null
evidence.observation: No static routes or policy-routing bypasses. eth1/eth2 carry only the declared data subnets; docker0 is down without an address. Forwarding is enabled globally and on both data interfaces, with rp_filter 0. SONiC's bgp container is up and bgpd listens on 179; dormant SONiC template neighbors remain inactive. No active capture/debug process was found; the remaining 232-byte /tmp/bgp-debug.log is a SONiC BGP startup log.
